stories.headline: EU AI Act High-Risk Provisions Go Live — Agentic AI Deployments Become a Compliance Matter Overnight
stories.summary: The EU AI Act's high-risk enforcement provisions, including mandatory risk management, human oversight, and conformity assessment, became enforceable on August 2, 2026, alongside transparency rules requiring AI agents to self-identify and synthetic media to carry watermarks. Non-compliance can trigger fines up to €15 million or 3% of global annual revenue, meaning enterprise agent deployments now carry board-level legal exposure — not just engineering risk. For D&B, this is a direct tailwind: regulated enterprises deploying agentic workflows will demand explainable, auditable ground-truth data, precisely the 'Explainability First' position D&B has been building toward.

stories.headline: Moody's Posts 15.1% Revenue Growth in Q2 2026, Validates AI-Powered Risk Data Premium
stories.summary: Moody's Corporation reported 15.1% revenue growth in Q2 2026, a strong signal that enterprise appetite for AI-enhanced credit and risk data intelligence is accelerating — not softening despite macro headwinds. The result reinforces the commercial value of owning proprietary risk data assets (ratings, Maxsight, private credit analytics) at a time when lenders and corporates need more granular, real-time decisioning data. D&B should track this closely: Moody's premium growth rate raises the competitive bar and underscores the valuation premium the market is assigning to data companies with defensible, proprietary content layers.

stories.headline: Alibaba's Accio Platform Gains Autonomous Sourcing Agents, Putting Entity and Supplier Data at the Centre of B2B Commerce
stories.summary: Alibaba upgraded Accio, its B2B sourcing platform, with agentic AI capabilities that can autonomously execute multi-step procurement tasks — moving well beyond assisted search. A concurrent startup, Sazo, is building an entire cross-border commerce infrastructure layer on the same autonomous-agent model. The development highlights a structural shift: as agentic sourcing moves supplier discovery accountability from the analyst to the platform, the quality and coverage of underlying entity and supplier data becomes the decisive differentiator — a gap D&B's DUNS-anchored corporate family trees and 600M+ business records are positioned to fill for any platform wanting to build on trusted entity resolution.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve's 2026 Small Business Credit Survey Finds Tariff Costs Hit 4-in-10 Firms, Revenue Outlook Falls
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve's 2026 Report on Employer Firms found that more than four in ten small businesses cited tariff-related cost increases as a financial challenge, with tariff pain most acute in retail (69%) and manufacturing (62%). Revenue and employment growth held steady in 2025, but forward-looking expectations have declined. This deteriorating SMB credit environment reinforces demand for real-time commercial data signals — payment behaviour, delinquency trends, trade credit exposure — exactly the domain where D&B's Paydex scores and trade data give lenders and credit managers an early-warning edge that backward-looking financial statements cannot provide.

stories.headline: Salesforce Frames Dreamforce 2026 Around the 'Agentic Enterprise' — Agentforce and Data 360 Take Centre Stage
stories.summary: Salesforce has confirmed Dreamforce 2026 for September 15–17 in San Francisco, structuring the entire event around what it calls the 'Agentic Enterprise' — autonomous AI agents operating at scale, with Data 360 and governance as the supporting pillars. The framing is a clear signal that Salesforce is doubling down on Agentforce as its primary enterprise GTM narrative heading into year-end selling cycles. For D&B, Dreamforce represents both a validation of the agentic platform strategy and a live commercial opportunity: deep Agentforce integration positions D&B data as the trusted entity and firmographic layer powering the very agents Salesforce will be showcasing to thousands of enterprise buyers.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer — Open-Weight Agent Model That Runs on a Single Laptop GPU
stories.summary: Meta released Muse Glimmer on August 10, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model distilled from Muse Spark 1.2 and licensed under Apache 2.0, designed to run local agentic workflows on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Zuckerberg paired the release with a 14-page essay urging Washington not to restrict open-source AI, framing it as a direct counter to Chinese open-weight models like DeepSeek. The move is strategically significant for D&B: as capable agent models move onto the device and away from the cloud, the premium on trusted, structured data — entity resolution, Paydex, corporate family trees — embedded at the agent layer grows, because the model itself becomes a commodity.

stories.headline: EU AI Act High-Risk Enforcement Now Live — Article 50 Transparency Obligations Took Effect August 2
stories.summary: The EU AI Act's next enforcement phase came into force on August 2, with the European Commission's AI Office and national authorities beginning active enforcement of Article 50 transparency obligations covering chatbot disclosure, synthetic content marking, and deepfake labelling. Notably, the Digital Omnibus signed on July 8 deferred full high-risk system compliance — covering credit scoring, recruitment tools, and law enforcement — to December 2027, giving enterprises a 17-month reprieve on those obligations. For D&B, the credit-scoring and insurance-pricing carve-out is directly relevant: explainability requirements under Articles 9, 12, and 14 will eventually land on customers using AI-driven risk decisions, making D&B's ground-truth data layer and audit trail a compliance asset, not just a commercial one.

stories.headline: US Federal AI Preemption Bill Stalls in House — State-Level Patchwork Accelerates
stories.summary: The US 'Great American AI Act,' which would have established federal preemption over state AI laws, has stalled in the House over the preemption clause, leaving California and Colorado enforcing their own rules. Simultaneously, China issued its first fines under new companion AI regulations — 12 companies receiving fines totalling 4.2 million RMB in the first week of enforcement. The fragmented US regulatory environment increases enterprise compliance complexity and reinforces demand for AI systems that carry documented, explainable data provenance — a direct tailwind for D&B's Explainability First positioning.

stories.headline: NVIDIA Launches New Business Model to Broaden Compute Access for AI Startups and Regional Players
stories.summary: NVIDIA announced on August 5 a new financing and access model specifically targeting AI startups, model builders, research organisations, and regional players who have historically been locked out of capital-intensive GPU infrastructure. The move comes as McKinsey projects AI-related data-centre infrastructure will require roughly $6.7 trillion in capital investment by 2030, and the IEA forecasts global data-centre electricity consumption will more than double to 945 terawatt-hours by 2030. Widening compute access matters for D&B's 'be everywhere' strategy: more funded, GPU-equipped AI startups building agentic workflows means more potential embedding points for D&B's data layer across a broader and faster-growing ecosystem.

stories.headline: US Dismantles Iran's Secret Financial Network in Major Sanctions Push
stories.summary: The US took steps on 7 August to dismantle networks that helped Iran secretly move hundreds of millions of dollars through the international financial system. The move comes as Trump publicly stated the US is only 'semi-negotiating' with Iran, and analysts warn a continued strait closure could push petrol prices sharply higher after a nine-cent-per-gallon drop last week. The standoff has direct implications for UK energy costs and global supply chains.

stories.headline: Starmer Government Faces Fresh Reform UK Pressure as Braverman Defects
stories.summary: Former Home Secretary Suella Braverman formally defected to Reform UK, becoming the latest high-profile Conservative to embrace Nigel Farage's platform. The move further fractures the right-of-centre vote and piles pressure on Labour ahead of what Farage has described as the most important set of elections before the next general election. Reform continues to lead in national opinion polls, with 35% of Britons now viewing them as best placed to handle immigration.

stories.headline: NASA Buys Voyager 2 More Time With 'Big Bang' Power Manoeuvre
stories.summary: NASA engineers have found a way to extend the operational life of Voyager 2, nearly 50 years after it left Earth. In an operation nicknamed the 'Big Bang,' the team simultaneously shut down onboard systems to free up power, keeping the probe's science instruments alive longer than previously expected. The feat is a remarkable piece of deep-space engineering as the probe continues its journey beyond the solar system.

stories.headline: Total Solar Eclipse to Plunge Spain and Parts of Europe Into Darkness on 12 August
stories.summary: A total solar eclipse will cross parts of Europe on Wednesday 12 August 2026, with Spain offering some of the best viewing conditions on the continent. The European Space Agency will livestream the event from the Javalambre Observatory, combining telescope feeds, drone footage, and expert commentary. It is the most significant celestial event visible from Europe in years and follows a strong week of Perseid meteor shower activity.

stories.headline: Arsenal Beaten Again in Pre-Season — Dortmund Down Gunners 3-2 at Emirates
stories.summary: Arsenal suffered a 2-3 pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates on 9 August, following their earlier loss to Real Betis. The back-to-back defeats will raise questions ahead of the Community Shield against Man City in Cardiff on 16 August, with the Premier League season starting on 22 August. Arsenal enter as defending champions but pre-season form has been patchy.

stories.headline: Nations Championship Era Begins: Six Nations Announces New Global Rivalry Format
stories.summary: The Six Nations organisation has officially unveiled the Nations Championship — a new global competition format designed to erase the traditional north-south divide in rugby. The announcement, made in June 2026, creates cross-hemisphere matchups between Six Nations sides and southern hemisphere nations, representing the most significant structural change to elite rugby union in decades. It arrives on the back of France's dramatic 48-46 Six Nations title win over England in March.

stories.headline: PGA Tour Player of the Year Race Goes Down to the Wire With Five Events Left
stories.summary: The 2026 PGA Tour Player of the Year award is shaping up to be one of the most contested in years, with five candidates still in contention and five events remaining in the season. Golf Channel analysts have been debating the merits of a wide-open field as the FedEx Cup Playoffs approach. Meanwhile, the DP World Tour's Danish Golf Championship tees off at Great Northern in Denmark from 13 August, offering European Tour points with the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth looming in September.

stories.headline: The Battle for Verifiable Data Is Defining the AI Race — Ben Thompson, Stratechery (July 9, 2026)
stories.summary: Thompson's update argues that the contest between Meta, Grok, and frontier labs is no longer purely about model capability — it is about who controls verifiable, real-world data. As models converge on benchmark performance, the differentiating asset shifts to proprietary data that can be independently validated and trusted. This is a direct validation of D&B's core moat: 600M+ business records, Paydex payment history, and DUNS entity resolution are exactly the kind of verifiable, structured ground-truth data that AI agents require to act reliably. Any enterprise AI workflow that cannot anchor decisions to verified entity data risks compounding errors at agent scale — making D&B's neutrality and data depth a strategic necessity, not a nice-to-have.

stories.headline: Dithering: 'Vibe-Porting and Meta Enterprise' — Ben Thompson & John Gruber (August 4, 2026)
stories.summary: Thompson and Gruber's August 4 Dithering episode examines Meta's push into enterprise AI, asking whether a consumer-native platform built on open-weights models can credibly displace established enterprise software vendors. The discussion surfaces a structural tension: enterprise buyers want accountability, auditability, and vendor stability, qualities Meta's open-source positioning makes harder to guarantee. For D&B, this is a meaningful signal — as more AI platforms compete for enterprise workflow share, the demand for a neutral, auditable data layer sitting above any single vendor grows stronger. D&B's 'be everywhere' strategy of embedding into all agentic platforms (Copilot, Agentforce, Gemini, Bedrock) hedges precisely against the fragmentation this episode describes.
stories.source: Ben Thompson & John Gruber, Dithering / Stratechery

stories.headline: AI Eats the World: Distribution and Product Wrapping Matter More Than Raw Model Capability — Benedict Evans (May 2026, widely recirculated August 2026)
stories.summary: Evans' flagship 2026 macro presentation argues that the decisive question in AI is not which model wins, but which companies can convert fast model progress into durable products, embedded workflows, and distribution advantages — because general-purpose technologies only become valuable through specific use cases, not demos or thin software wrappers. He notes hyperscalers committed a combined $650B in AI capex for 2026, yet consumer daily active usage remains shallow, flagging a gap between infrastructure spend and genuine adoption depth. For D&B, Evans' framework is directly affirming: proprietary structured data assets embedded at the workflow level (entity resolution, corporate family trees, Paydex scores surfaced inside Copilot or Agentforce) is exactly the 'specific use case' wrapping Evans identifies as where durable value accrues. The analysis also reinforces that model commoditisation strengthens the relative value of verified data and distribution — both D&B strengths.

data_science.tagline: The single source of truth for ML features — computed once, shared everywhere, always consistent.
data_science.what_it_is: A Feature Store is a centralised data system that manages the full lifecycle of ML features: computation, storage, versioning, and serving. It sits between raw data pipelines and ML models, acting as a shared library of reusable, production-ready features. The key insight is that features are expensive to build correctly — cleaning, joining, aggregating, validating — and without a feature store, every team rebuilds the same logic independently, introducing drift, duplication, and training/serving skew. A feature store solves this by separating 'feature engineering' from 'model training', so a feature computed for a fraud model can be instantly reused for a credit risk model with zero rework. Modern feature stores (Feast, Tecton, Hopsworks, Databricks Feature Store) provide two serving paths: an offline store (columnar, e.g. Parquet/Delta Lake) for batch training, and an online store (low-latency key-value, e.g. Redis/DynamoDB) for real-time inference — both guaranteed to return identical feature values.
data_science.how_it_works: 1. DEFINE: Features are declared as code — a feature spec names the entity key (e.g. company DUNS number), the source table, the transformation logic, and the freshness SLA. 2. COMPUTE: A materialisation job (Spark, dbt, Flink) runs the transformation and writes results to both the offline store (historical snapshots) and the online store (latest values). 3. RETRIEVE (Training): A 'point-in-time correct' join fetches the exact feature value that existed at each training label's timestamp — this prevents data leakage where future information bleeds into past labels. 4. RETRIEVE (Inference): At prediction time, the model fetches features from the low-latency online store via entity key in <10ms. 5. MONITOR: The store tracks feature statistics (mean, null rate, distribution) over time, alerting on drift before it silently degrades model performance. The point-in-time join is the most technically critical piece — it ensures that when you train on 'company X's Paydex score in January 2024', you use the score that actually existed in January 2024, not the score that was later backdated or corrected.
data_science.when_to_use: Use a feature store when: (a) you have more than 2–3 ML models in production and feature logic is being copy-pasted between pipelines; (b) you need real-time inference and can't afford to recompute features on the fly at serving time; (c) training/serving skew is causing unexplained model degradation in production; (d) compliance or explainability requires an auditable record of exactly which feature values drove a specific prediction; (e) you have a platform team supporting multiple data science squads who should share features rather than diverge. A feature store is overkill for a single prototype model but becomes essential infrastructure once ML is a repeated, multi-team capability. The ROI is highest in environments with high-cardinality entity keys (millions of companies, contacts) and features that are expensive to compute — exactly D&B's situation.
data_science.worked_example: D&B context — 'Propensity-to-Buy' agent across 600M+ business records. The Prospecting Agent needs to score every company in a territory on likelihood to buy a D&B data product in the next 90 days. Without a feature store, each squad recomputes features like: rolling 12-month Paydex trajectory, corporate family tree depth, employee growth rate, firmographic segment, and number of recent ownership changes. With a feature store keyed on DUNS number: (1) these features are computed nightly by a single Spark job and written to the offline store (Delta Lake) and online store (Redis); (2) the Prospecting Agent calls the online store with a list of DUNS numbers and gets all five features back in <15ms per entity; (3) the Account Expansion Agent reuses the same 'Paydex trajectory' and 'ownership change' features for churn risk scoring — zero extra engineering; (4) when a sales rep asks the AI 'why did this company score 94?', the feature store provides an audit log of the exact feature values and timestamps used — this is D&B's 'Explainability First / Ground Truth' principle made operational; (5) point-in-time joins ensure the model trained on Q1 2025 data used the Paydex scores that existed in Q1 2025, not today's updated values, eliminating leakage. The feature store becomes the connective tissue that makes all six D&B agent archetypes consistent, auditable, and fast.
resources: Feast open-source feature store documentation — feast.dev — the most widely used open-source implementation, covers offline/online store architecture and point-in-time joins in depth

'Rethinking Feature Stores' by Tecton (tecton.ai/blog) — practical deep-dive into training/serving skew, materialisation patterns, and real-time feature pipelines from the team that built Uber's Michelangelo
'Designing Machine Learning Systems' by Chip Huyen (O'Reilly, 2022) — Chapter 7 covers feature engineering and feature stores with rigorous treatment of data leakage and point-in-time correctness
